- \`.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md\` and its guide twin now mention the setting and \`alwaysOn\`.

The dialog with shortcuts turned off, in the light and dark themes:

<img alt="Keyboard shortcuts dialog with the checkbox cleared and every row but Show keyboard shortcuts greyed, light theme" src="https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/$SHA/docs/sprint2/screenshots/60-shortcuts-off-light.png?raw=1" width="420"> <img alt="The same dialog, dark theme" src="https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/$SHA/docs/sprint2/screenshots/60-shortcuts-off-dark.png?raw=1" width="420">

## Why

WCAG 2.1.4 requires a way to turn single-character shortcuts off. Without one, a speech recognition user can set off \`s\`, \`g i\` and the others just by dictating a word.

- AC1: with the box cleared, \`s\`, \`t\`, \`g …\`, \`c\` and \`r\` do nothing. The key isn't default-prevented, so focus stays where it was.
- AC2: the setting lives in \`localStorage\`, so it holds across reloads and other pages in the same browser.
- AC3: \`?\` is always on. The dialog still opens, and a keyboard user can Tab to the checkbox and press Space.
- AC4: checking the box again turns shortcuts back on right away, with no reload.
- AC5: if storage throws, shortcuts start on and the checkbox still works for that page.
- AC6: with shortcuts off, \`g\` doesn't start a sequence, and turning them off drops a sequence already started.
- AC7: the label comes from \`shortcuts.help.enable\`.
- AC8: see the tests below.

## How it was tested

- \`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts\` has seven new tests, each named for the ACs it covers. They check that keys run nothing with the setting off (AC1) while \`?\` still runs (AC3), the two \`g\` sequence cases (AC6), and that a new registry reads the stored value the way the next page load would (AC2, AC4). They also cover storage that throws (AC5), and the dialog's checkbox turning shortcuts off and on with only \`?\` left undimmed.
- \`tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts\` has a new test that turns shortcuts off from the keyboard and reloads. It checks that \`s\` does nothing and \`?\` still opens the dialog, then turns shortcuts back on and checks that \`s\` focuses search (AC2, AC3, AC4).
- The grey rows and the checkbox's position can only be checked by eye, so I looked at both in the light and dark themes. That's how I caught the checkbox sitting outside the dialog's padding.

## CI / manual verification

\`\`\`sh
pnpm exec vitest run web_src/js/modules/shortcut
GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts' make test-e2e
\`\`\`

- All 34 shortcut unit tests pass. eslint, tsc, stylelint and the template linter report nothing.
- All 54 shortcut e2e tests pass in Chromium and WebKit on top of \`main\`, including #59's \`c\` and #95's \`r\`. Firefox hangs at launch on macOS 27, so CI is its first run.
- In a running Gitea I turned shortcuts off from the keyboard and checked that \`s\`, \`g i\` and \`c\` did nothing and that the setting survived a reload. Then I turned them back on with \`?\` and Space.

## Design

This follows both Design Decisions in #60: the setting is stored in the browser with \`localUserSettings\` (Decision 1), and \`?\` stays on as the way back, with a code comment saying why (Decision 2).

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The setting is per browser, as Decision 1 chose, so someone who wants shortcuts off on two machines has to turn them off twice. The dialog is the only place to change it. The issue leaves a copy on the settings pages out of scope.

**Encountered:** When the dialog closes, Chromium can deliver the next key before the dialog's \`close\` event moves focus back to the page. That key lands on the checkbox, and the field check ignores it. Nobody types that fast, but the e2e test has to wait for focus to leave the checkbox, and a comment there explains the wait.

metadata:

---

Built 2026-10-06. It's all local-only, because `.claude/` is gitignored. The rules themselves are in `ai-logs/README.md`.

- **`.claude/bin/ai-log <slug> [session-id] [--sprint N] [--dry-run]`, and `--list`:**
  - Runs `specstory sync claude -s <id> --no-cloud-sync`.
  - Finds the transcript by its `<!-- Claude Code Session <id> (...Z) -->` header, looking only in the first 5 lines because transcripts quote other sessions' ids.
  - Copies it byte for byte to `ai-logs/sprint<N>/controlled-opposition/<LOCAL start date>_claude-code_<slug>.md`.
  - A dry run reproduced all four hand-filed logs exactly.
- **Sprint table:** the `SPRINTS` dates come from the course schedule, fetched 2026-10-06: S0 09-01..09-17, S1 09-22..10-08, S2 10-13..10-29, S3 11-03..11-19, S4 11-24..12-15. S4 ends Dec 15 per /schedule/; /sprints/ says Dec 10. A date between sprints errors out and needs `--sprint`.
- **Sync hook:** `.claude/settings.local.json` has a SessionEnd hook that runs `.claude/bin/specstory-sync-hook`, which syncs the ending session into `.specstory/history/`.
- **`/file-ai-logs` skill:**
  - lists unfiled sessions, skips the current one and command-only ones, and proposes slugs
  - files them after the user's OK and commits only with approval
  - drafts the issue comment

SpecStory quirks:
- Pass `--no-cloud-sync`; `sync` otherwise uploads to SpecStory Cloud when logged in.
- Don't use `--print`, which writes an "Update Available" banner to stdout.
- SpecStory's own filename can take its slug from a subagent prompt (#61 exported as `…-you-are-reviewing-uncommitted.md`). Trust the session-id header, not the name.
- An export made mid-session stops at the export command. Rerun it after the session ends; it overwrites the same file.
- Some exported lines are CRLF. `.gitattributes` normalises them on commit, so ignore git's warning.
- The existing logs are verbatim exports. Never hand-write or summarise a log.

**Why:** Hand-copying logs was error-prone (UTC vs local dates, auto-generated slugs), and edited or incomplete logs are graded invalid.
Sprint 2 grading strictly enforces linking **the log file itself** (not a folder or another issue) and full prompts plus output. See [[sprint2-requirements]].

**How to apply:** File logs with the script or skill, never by hand. Update `SPRINTS` when the schedule changes. See [[which-sessions-to-log]].

name: which-sessions-to-log
description: "File only sessions the course requires a log for (ones behind an issue's AI Assistance comment); never chase other unfiled sessions."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 71e5d7cd-352f-452d-834f-e857549a2dc3
  modified: 2026-10-22T19:00:00.000Z
---

Only care about sessions the class requires a log for: those that produced an issue deliverable that carries an AI Assistance comment. That means drafting an issue spec, implementing it, reviewing a PR or spec, and writing the sprint report. Everything else needs no log and no mention: general planning, "what are my issues" questions, requirement Q&A, memory questions, AI tooling setup (pstack, verify skill, ai-log, SpecStory), and empty or `/clear` sessions. The user said so on 2026-10-06 (tooling) and on 2026-10-22: "not every single session in existence needs to be filed."

**Why:** Over-logging clutters the graded record, and listing every unfiled session as a to-do wastes the user's attention.
**How to apply:** When filing, consider only sessions tied to the issue or PR in question. Don't list other unfiled sessions as leftovers or remind the user about them. A short planning session that leads straight into one issue's work may go with that issue's logs, but only if the user wants it. When unsure, ask. See [[ai-log-tooling]].
